title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: Mr. Lopez has a choice of two routes to get to work. Route A is \(6\) miles long, and his average speed along this route is \(30\) miles per hour. Route B is \(5\) miles long, and his average speed along this route is \(40\) miles per hour, except for a \(\tfrac{1}{2}\)-mile stretch in a school zone where his average speed is \(20\) miles per hour. By how many minutes is Route B quicker than Route A?

solutions.text:
Route A takes \(\dfrac{6}{30} = \dfrac{1}{5}\) hour \(= 12\) minutes.

Route B has \(4.5\) miles at \(40\) mph and \(0.5\) mile at \(20\) mph, taking \(\dfrac{4.5}{40} + \dfrac{0.5}{20}\) \(= 0.1125 + 0.025\) \(= 0.1375\) hour \(= 8.25\) minutes.

The difference is \(12 - 8.25 = 3.75 = 3\tfrac{3}{4}\) minutes.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Route A takes \(\dfrac{6}{30}\) hour; convert to minutes
Route B splits into \(4.5\) miles at \(40\) mph and \(0.5\) mile at \(20\) mph
